excerpt.text: At eight I put on the coat.

excerpt: It smelled faintly of someone else – a warm, green perfume, fig or something like it, and under that, salt.
In the right-hand pocket there was a hair tie with a single long dark hair wound round it, and three pieces of sea glass, pale green, worn as smooth as sweets.

excerpt.text: I put them back exactly as I’d found them.

caption:
Three weeks on a Cornish headland. A red coat on the hook by the door. And something of hers in every pocket.
